links.outcome: LLM pipeline discrimination (AUC) versus traditional ML baselines for ED return visit admission at two sites
links.effect: At WCM Gemini ICL AUC 0.746 vs CatBoost 0.723 (DeLong p=0.044); at VUMC logistic regression AUC 0.799 matched GPT-5 mini 0.789 (n.s.).
links.quote: The LLM-based pipeline outperformed the strongest traditional ML baseline at WCM (Gemini ICL = 3 AUC 0.746 vs. CatBoost AUC 0.723; DeLong p = 0.044), but not at VUMC, where logistic regression on structured data alone (AUC 0.799) matched the best LLM configuration (GPT-5 mini AUC 0.789, n.s.).

links.outcome: Cross-site variation in AI model performance across two academic medical centers
links.effect: Absolute discrimination at VUMC was higher than at WCM for both approaches; LLM advantage over baseline present at WCM but not VUMC.
links.quote: Absolute discrimination at VUMC was higher than at WCM for both approaches, indicating that the cross-site difference reflects local documentation and structured-data informativeness rather than LLM failure.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating per-encounter token consumption and data requirements as deployment feasibility axes for LLM pipelines

screen.reason: Retrospective multi-site evaluation of an LLM-based clinical prediction pipeline assessing feasibility constraints (accuracy, token cost, hallucination risk across sites), but does not test a specific operational guardrail or deployment practice.
